This confirms the full picture. I have everything needed to answer.

## What happens when an org owner downgrades their plan

**Who is allowed.** The billing page (`src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/billing/page.tsx`) gates the whole page on `can(actor, "org:manage_billing", {kind: "billing", orgId})`. `can()` lives in `src/lib/permissions.ts` and consults `ROLE_MATRIX`, where `org:manage_billing` requires role `"owner"` — the highest rank — with no ownership-escalation override, so only the org owner (not an admin/member/viewer) can reach this action. The action itself, `changePlanAction` in `src/actions/billing/change-plan.ts`, re-checks the same `can()` call, and the service layer underneath (`changePlan` in `src/server/services/billing-service.ts`) re-checks again via `assertCan`, so authorization is enforced three times on the same path (UI gate, action, service).

**What is compared against what.** Submitting the form calls `changePlanAction` → the wrapped handler in `change-plan.ts`. Before touching anything, `assertPlanFitsCurrentUsage()` calls `getUsage(actor, orgId)` (`usage-service.ts`) to pull live counters (seats/projects/storage used) and compares each against the **target** (smaller) plan's ceilings from `getPlanLimits()`/`wouldExceedLimit()` in `src/config/plan-limits.ts`, using a requested delta of `0` — i.e. "does what's already in use still fit the new plan?". If any dimension is already over the new plan's limit, it throws `PlanLimitError` and the downgrade is refused before any write happens. `changePlan()` in `billing-service.ts` performs the identical check again (seats/projects/storage/webhooks) as a second, service-level gate before writing.

**Where the plan is recorded and what's authoritative.** If both checks pass, `subscriptionRepo.updateSubscriptionPlan(orgId, plan, interval)` (`src/server/repositories/subscription-repository.ts`) updates the `subscriptions` table row — this is the only place the new plan is persisted. The code is explicit about this: the comment above `planFor()` in `billing-service.ts` states "the subscription row is the authority on which plan an org is on; the denormalised `organizations.plan` column is only a display convenience." Critically, `organization-repository.ts`'s `updateOrg()` never sets the `plan` column at all — it's written once, at org creation (`insertOrg`), and is otherwise immutable through the app's normal update paths. So after a downgrade, `subscriptions.plan` = new (smaller) plan, but `organizations.plan` stays frozen at whatever it was when the org was created.

**What happens afterwards.** `changePlan()` emits a `billing.plan_changed` event via `emit()` (`src/lib/event-bus.ts`) with `from`/`to` plan and actor info. Two listeners react: `activity-service.ts` records it to the audit log (`"changed the plan"`), and `webhook-service.ts`'s `registerWebhookListeners()` enqueues it for delivery to any org webhook endpoints. Back in `change-plan.ts`, `revalidateTagged([orgTag(orgId)], CACHE_PROFILES.hours)` invalidates the Next.js cache tag for that org so billing-page data refreshes.

**Where behavior diverges away from the billing pages.** This is the consequential part: almost every quota/entitlement check *outside* billing reads `org.plan` (the stale, never-updated `organizations.plan` column) rather than `subscription.plan`. Concretely: `attachment-service.ts` (storage quota), `invitation-service.ts` (seat quota on invites), `issue-service.ts` (issues-per-project quota), `project-service.ts` (project quota), `webhook-service.ts` (webhook count and the `webhooks` feature flag gate), `feature-flag-service.ts`'s `buildFlagContext()` (which decides which flags like `advanced_search`/`ai_issue_summary` are enabled via `planAtLeast()` in `plan-limits.ts`), plus `notification-service.ts`, `search-service.ts`, and `activity-service.ts`'s own flag-context builders — all pull `org.plan` from `organization-service.ts`/`organization-repository.ts`, not the subscription. Even `usage-service.ts`'s `recomputeUsage()` job checks warn-thresholds against `getPlanLimits(org.plan)`. The dashboard shell (`(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/layout.tsx`) explicitly documents this as an "invariant" — "the flag snapshot was evaluated against that organization's plan" — computing `snapshotFlags(buildFlagContext(actor, org))` from the same stale `org.plan` on every navigation.

So the practical effect of a downgrade: the billing page itself (`getBillingSummary`, which calls `planFor()` and prefers the subscription row) immediately shows the new, cheaper plan and its correct meters/invoice estimate. But everywhere else — issue creation limits, project creation limits, seat-invite limits, storage limits, webhook counts and the webhooks feature gate, and which premium feature flags are enabled — continues to enforce the **old, bigger** plan's limits, because those code paths read the never-updated `organizations.plan` column. (Only the `trial-expiry-job.ts` downgrade path and org creation ever wrote a plan value onto that column historically, and neither backfills it on a manual billing-page downgrade.) One additional wrinkle: `src/lib/rate-limit.ts` exposes `setOrgPlan()` to scale API-rate-limit buckets by plan, but nothing in the codebase ever calls it, so the rate limiter is permanently stuck defaulting to the free-plan ceiling regardless of actual plan — a pre-existing, unrelated dead code path rather than something the downgrade itself changes.
